tutorial: Assembly_Workbench.md, section "Example crank and slider" (the built-in Assembly workbench has no tutorial page of its own: Tutorial_KinematicAssembly.md is for the external Assembly3 workbench; the workbench page carries this example with the parts' Python). The parts are built with part_primitive / part_boolean from that Python's numbers, then the page's steps: assembly, ground the Base, Revolute Base-Crank, Slider Base-SliderRod, Revolute Crank-ConnectingRod, Cylindrical ConnectingRod-SliderRod.

expected.volumesNote: Crank and ConnectingRod worked out by hand from the page's sizes; Base and SliderRod not worked out (overlapping fuses) — read them once and keep.
expected.degreesOfFreedom: 1 (the crank's turn) by counting: 3 moving parts x 6 = 18, less revolute 5 + slider 5 + revolute 5 + cylindrical 4 = 19, plus the 2 redundantly held the wiki page names. FreeCAD 1.1 does not report freedom left through Python (solve() returns 0, -1 or -6 only), so no tool can read this number: it is shown by CrankPivot still turning.
expected.fits: every pin 8 mm in a hole 8 mm: clearance 0, H7/g6 verdict fix
